jobs.title: Dewatering Supervisor (Fort Knox, AK, US)
jobs.description:
Located approximately 26 miles from the City of Fairbanks, Fort Knox is a centre of excellence for the Company as one of the few cold weather heap leach facilities in the world.

Fort Knox

celebrated its 25-year anniversary

in 2021, and has produced over 8.5 million ounces since it began operation. In 2020, Kinross acquired Manh Choh – a project expected to commence production in 2024 and process ore at Fort Knox.

Fort Knox prioritizes being a strong contributor to the State and local communities, and since 2001, has helped support more than 300 community partners and has contributed more than US$25 million to the Alaska Mental Health Trust.

Job Description

Dewatering Supervisor is responsible for supervising and instructing the Dewatering crew; maintaining the dewatering system in an effort to ensure water levels remain below current mining levels; maintain water storage levels and access for seasonal dust suppression needs; perform all aspects of the position in a, safe, cost-effective, and productive manner while continuously aligning daily functions to reflect Kinross’ values.

Job Responsibilities

Line out crews in a way they can effectively achieve all production goals.

Develop and maintain the mine dewatering programs.

Coordinate all maintenance activities of the dewatering infrastructure to include wells, pumping stations, piezometers, piping, transformers, power cables etc.

Conduct performance evaluations, recommend promotions, and carry out disciplinary actions as needed.

Investigate, analyze and supervise the documentation of accidents, injuries, and equipment damage and recommend prevention strategies as necessary.

Work with mine planning to schedule upcoming projects.  Assist the Technical Services Department with determining specifications of the equipment.

Coordinate with the mine and mill departments on production goals and priorities.

Coordinate with planning and warehousing to ensure that all necessary parts, tools, and equipment are available to complete work assignments efficiently.

Interface with various equipment manufacturers’ representatives.

Monitor work areas on an ongoing basis to assure a safe and efficient operation.

Report Processing: daily time cards, Paid Time Off (PTO) requests, accident and injury reports, and disciplinary action reports.

Control expenditures and lost production by minimizing equipment downtime through properly executed preventative maintenance and repairs.

Answers queries and handles requests concerning health and safety, production, mechanical/electrical training and development, and supervisory skills.

Works closely with the Maintenance Planners to schedule equipment repairs and replacement to maximize equipment utilization and minimize downtime.

Helps develop other department personnel to perform duties listed above.

Compliance with all company policies and procedures including, but not limited to safety, environmental, confidentiality and code of conduct.

Meets or exceeds established performance expectations set by management.

Consistently exercises discretion and judgment in job performance.

Works without risk or harm to self and others.

Possession of a valid driver’s license issued by state agency.

Punctuality and regular attendance required.

Perform other related functions as assigned by supervisor.

Education and Experience

Education

A Bachelor of Science in hydrology or mechanical engineering is preferred.

Experience

Strong mechanical background.

Previous mine dewatering experience desired.

Skills

Employee must have sufficient education to read and write instructions, perform simple mathematical calculations, and keep records.

General understanding of mining operations, as well as limited understanding of milling and maintenance operations.

Good working knowledge and skill with P.C. utilizing word processing, spreadsheet, database, and presentation software.

Strong verbal, written, analytical, and persuasive skills and the ability to interact effectively with all levels of employees and management.

Demonstrates strong administrative, organizational and technical writing skills.

Must be a self-starter with the ability to work with others in a team environment.

Ability to function within the qualifications outlined in the attached physical demands sheets.

May work holidays, weekends, and shift work as required.

Reporting Relationships

This role reports to the Water Treatment and Utilities General Supervisor 

Legislative Requirements

US work permit required

Language Requirements

English

Travel Requirements

Travel not required, only exceptionally

jobs.title: Senior Mine Engineer (Elko, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Bald Mountain is an open-pit mine with a large estimated mineral resource in the largest private mining land package in the U.S. The mine is located in White Pine County, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world, along the southern extension of the prolific Carlin trend. Bald Mountain and the nearby Round Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

Bald Mountain is an important contributor to the economy of northeastern Nevada and maintains a comprehensive environmental strategy including wildlife protection, habitat recovery and education.

Job Summary

Responsible for carrying out a full range of engineering functions including but not limited to; development of an accurate mine plan, evaluating assumptions and production rates, pit design updates, analyzing equipment needs, managing multiple projects, creation of alternative mine plans and scenarios, and evaluation of various options with the goal of maximizing revenue in alignment with developed Forecasts, Budget and Life of Mine plans and schedules. Must show the ability and willingness to supervise, manage performance and development of department personnel. Will have direct involvement and integration with staff from all departments. Will integrate across the mining value chain to ensure optimal; utilization of resources and personnel; and maximize productivity.

Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

Essential Functions

1.  Develop and/or oversee short-term (daily, weekly and monthly) plans based on reserve and ore control models, production budgets, and forecasts. 
2.  Generate medium term and forecast mine plans in coordination with other departments as required, ensuring alignment with the overall budget plan. 
3.  Provide input for long-term and LOM plan coordination. 
4.  Mentor and develop direct reports to ensure optimal performance of the section.
5.  Manage performance of direct reports and identify opportunities for maximizing strengths and for areas of development.
6.  Evaluate alternative designs and mine plans based on various operational scenarios with the goal of maximizing productivity and revenue.
7.  Conduct equipment studies to verify that planned production goals can be met.
8.  Make recommendations for opportunities that maximize efficiency and productivity of the entire operation.
9.  Complete federal and state permit compliance reports or documentation as required.
10.  Represent the company in requests for bids for capital earthwork and site construction jobs.
11.  Design or generate maps, as-built, bench plans, cross-sections, or permit drawings as required.
12.  Monitor monthly production. Provide current pit topography from monthly mine advance surveys or aerial surveys.
13.  Integrate with up and downstream disciplines and processes to ensure consideration in planning and reconciliation processes. 
14.  Coordinate interdepartmental activities that directly impact daily production targets.
15.  Generate mine planning and project management monthly summaries for use in company reporting.
16.  Provide support, as needed, to other departments on monthly reporting.
17.  Review designs of dumps, access roads, ramps, and mine site facilities.
18.  Project management duties, including, but not limited to; assisting with operational and capital project teams as required. 
19.  Consistent exercise of discretion and judgment in job performance.
20.  Punctuality and regular attendance is required.
21.  Meet or exceed established performance expectations set by management.
22.  Compliance with all company policies and procedures including, but not limited to, safety, confidentiality, and environmental policies.
23.  Possession of a valid driver’s license issued by the state.

25.  Work without significant risk of harm to self and others.

1.  BS Degree in engineering from an ABET accredited program  
2.  Minimum of five years of experience in an open pit mining environment preferred.
3.  Knowledge of engineering techniques as they apply to pit design, mine planning, equipment analysis, and project management.
4.  Thorough understanding of open-pit mining operations as well as a general understanding of heap leaching process and mine maintenance.

jobs.title: UG Senior Safety Specialist (Bald Mountain, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Bald Mountain is an open-pit mine with a large estimated mineral resource in the largest private mining land package in the U.S. The mine is located in White Pine County, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world, along the southern extension of the prolific Carlin trend. Bald Mountain is an important contributor to the economy of northeastern Nevada and maintains a comprehensive environmental strategy including wildlife protection, habitat recovery and education.

Job Summary

Under the direction of the TOP UG Project Manager, the Senior Safety Specialist supports the TOP UG Exploration Project and MSHA-regulated health and safety programs. As a subject matter expert in hazard identification, risk mitigation, and emergency preparedness, the incumbent works collaboratively across all departments to integrate safety into daily operations. Aligned with Kinross’s Safeground Ethos, this role simplifies safe work, promotes a fail-safe environment, and fosters a speak-up culture where people are the solution, and continuous learning drives safe outcomes.

Essential Functions

·  Ensure compliance with all applicable MSHA, federal, state, and company safety regulations.
·  Conduct regular inspections, audits, and risk assessments across the TOP UG Project; track and follow up on corrective actions.
·  Lead investigations of incidents and near-misses; analyze root causes and recommend preventative measures.
·  Develop and deliver safety training programs for employees and contractors, including annual MSHA Part 48 refresher requirements.
·  Assist in establishing goals and objectives regarding the development and implementation of Health and Safety programs.
·  Maintain and review safety documentation including training records, inspection logs, and incident reports.
·  Assist in developing and updating the site’s Safety Management System (SMS) and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
·  Responsible for Fire Prevention Officer duties.
·  Support Industrial Hygiene (IH)/Occupational Health (OH) programs and coordinate monitoring as required.
·  Prepare and submit required MSHA documentation and reports.
·  Participate in emergency response drills and assist in updating site emergency response plans.
·  Collaborate with operational leadership on job hazard analyses (JHAs), change management, and risk assessments.
·  Establish and maintain good relations with peers, supervisors, and employees and promote positive attitudes, safe work practices and adherence to safe work standards. 
·  Lead by example, provide guidance, and motivate employees to work safely.
·  Comply with all company policies and procedures.
·  Meet or exceed the performance expectations established by management. 
·  Punctuality and regular attendance required. 
·  Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Skills

•  Bachelor’s degree in a relevant discipline, or suitable combination of experience and education.
•  5+ years of experience working in Health and Safety. 3 years of experience in an MSHA regulated environment. Underground hardrock mining experience required. 
•  Applied knowledge of relevant OSHA, MSHA, state and other regulatory requirements, as-well-as industry standards and practices. 
•  MSHA Part 48 “blue card” certified trainer.
•  Certified Safety Professional (CSP) or similar experience.
•  Proven experience conducting investigations, hazard assessments, and safety training.
•  Strong written and verbal communication, interpersonal and analytical skills. 
•  Capability to work in both office and field environments.
•  Experienced using MS Office software (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, and Teams).
•  Requires valid US driver’s license.

Health, Safety, and Environmental Requirements

•  Adheres to all safety and environmental considerations.
•  Has a strong commitment to safe working practices. 
•  Wears Personal Protective Equipment at all times while in the production environment. 
•  Is alert and observes, corrects, and reports unsafe conditions.

•  Creates an environment where nothing is more important than every employee returning home safe and healthy every day.

jobs.title: IT Specialist (Elko, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Bald Mountain is an open-pit mine with a large estimated mineral resource in the largest private mining land package in the U.S. The mine is located in White Pine County, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world, along the southern extension of the prolific Carlin trend. Bald Mountain and the nearby Round Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

Bald Mountain is an important contributor to the economy of northeastern Nevada and maintains a comprehensive environmental strategy including wildlife protection, habitat recovery and education.

Job Summary

The IT Specialist is a hands‑on, customer‑focused technologist who keeps Bald Mountain’s users productive and our site technology resilient. You’ll split time between first‑line/second‑line support and ownership of core systems: Windows servers/Active Directory, IGA (Identity Governance and Administration), Nutanix‑based virtualization and storage, Cisco switching and fiber, point‑to‑point and point‑to‑multipoint wireless links, and Dell client endpoints. You’ll also collaborate with OT and plant teams to support industrial networks and site infrastructure.

Essential Functions

End‑user support & customer service

•    Serve as a primary contact for the North America Service Desk; resolve incidents/requests for Windows 11, Windows Server 2019 and newer, O365, Teams, Printing, VPN, and core business apps with high first‑time‑fix rates.
•    Provide one‑on‑one and small‑group end‑user training; write how‑to guides and knowledge base articles.

Server/virtualization & storage

•    Administer Windows Server/AD, DNS/DHCP, GPO, and patching; monitor backups and recovery procedures.
•    Operate Nutanix‑based clusters (compute/storage/virtualization) and site NAS/SAN (Dell/Synology); perform capacity and health checks and coordinate upgrades with vendors.

Network / Wireless / Telephony

•    Maintain and administer campus/industrial Ethernet (Cisco) switching, VLANs, QoS, link aggregation, and optics; ensure fiber plant integrity and documentation.
•    Support site point‑to‑point and point‑to‑multipoint wireless systems (backhaul and access), including design inputs, LOS checks, and alignment/validation.
•    Support for Cisco Desk Telephones and Teleconference Systems including Cisco desk telephones and teleconference systems.

OT & site technology

•    Partner with Operational and Support Departments on industrial networks, historian/SCADA connectivity, and change management that protects safety and uptime.

Lifecycle, documentation & compliance

•    Own device imaging/provisioning for Dell laptops/workstations; manage asset inventory and lifecycle.
•    Follow site safety and LOTOTO practices; complete required MSHA new‑miner training; adhere to Kinross Americas Safety Guidelines in all work.
•    Contribute to change records and diagrams; keep runbooks, network maps, and rack elevations current.

On‑call & field work

•    Participate in after‑hours and weekend support rotation; travel to comm sites and facilities around the property as needed (all weather).

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

•    3+ years in IT support/operations with demonstrated customer service mindset.
•    Solid skills with Windows client/Server, AD, DNS/DHCP, GPO, and endpoint management; strong troubleshooting across OS/app/network stacks.
•    Hands‑on experience with Cisco switching and fiber (port/VLAN provisioning, SFPs, optics, link testing).
•    Working knowledge of wireless links (P2P/PMP) and fundamentals like RSSI/SNR, alignment, and link budgets.
•    Familiarity with virtualization and enterprise storage (Nutanix preferred) and backup/recovery workflows.
•    Ability to create and deliver clear user training and concise documentation.
•    Valid driver’s license; ability to safely work at heights/rack spaces and lift up to ~50 lbs; willingness to work outdoors in a mine environment.
•    Demonstrated ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise sound judgment when handling sensitive business or personal information.
•    Commitment to ethical conduct and compliance with Kinross data protection and privacy standards.

Preferred Experience

•    Certifications: CompTIA A+/Network+, CCNA, Microsoft MD‑102/Windows, AZ‑104, Nutanix NCP.
•    Experience in OT/industrial networks and CPwE concepts; exposure to SCADA/historian connectivity.
•    Scripting/automation (PowerShell), imaging tools, and endpoint security/patching platforms.
•    Familiar with JDE system for equipment procurement.

Health, Safety, and Environmental Requirements

•    Complies with all Kinross & Nevada sites health, safety and environmental policies and procedures.
•    Have a strong commitment to safe working practices. 
•    Is alert and observes, corrects, and reports unsafe conditions. 
•    Follows operating procedures and complies with all regulatory requirements.

Develop and communicate rigorous and creative business strategies that drive sustainable value.
•    External Engagement
Understand and build relationships with external parties that strengthen and sustain competitive advantage.
•    Business Focus
Apply commercial rigor and discipline to all business decisions and customer relationships.
•    Living the Kinross Values
Align personal behavior, decisions, and actions with Kinross values and principles.

jobs.title: Round Mountain: Part-time Relief Operator (Round Mountain, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Round Mountain is an open-pit mine located in Nevada, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world. The mine uses conventional open-pit mining methods and processes ore by mill and heap leach. Kinross began operating the mine in 2003, and it has since become a continuous improvement leader in the Company’s portfolio. Round Mountain poured its 15 millionth ounce in 2018. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Summary

We are seeking candidates interested in a
part-time Relief Operator position
operating off-road haul trucks in an active mine environment. 

This position will work a
7-on / 7-off schedule, approximately 9 hours per shift
, with employees assigned to either
straight day shift or straight night shift
. Employees will not rotate between days and nights. The schedule will not exceed
130 hours per month
.

Employees are responsible for commuting to and from the mine site. Company medical insurance is not provided for this position; however, an
insurance stipend may be available
for employees who do not have access to other medical coverage.

Relief Drivers must be able to work effectively both independently and as part of the Operations team and be willing to adapt to changing priorities, assignments, and operating conditions. All work must be performed safely and efficiently while demonstrating Kinross’ values in day-to-day responsibilities.

jobs.title: Intermediate Instrumentation & Control Engineer (Red Lake, ON, CA)
jobs.description:
The Great Bear project is a development-stage asset located in the renowned and prolific Red Lake mining district, and represents one of the most exciting recent gold discoveries globally.  The project has excellent potential to become a top-tier deposit that could support a large, long-life mine complex. Kinross’ comprehensive exploration and development program will aim to support the vision of a quality, high-grade, open-pit mine and a longer-term, sizeable underground mine.

Job Summary

The Intermediate Instrumentation and Control Engineer will assist the Instrumentation and Control Lead with engineering review of the instrumentation and control related work associated with the Great Bear Project, in particular process plant instrumentation and process control, utilities, water management instrumentation and process control, mining services and other infrastructure on surface and underground during Detailed Engineering.

Key Responsibilities and Duties

Conduct thorough reviews of vendor documents and comment on a wide range of technical documents including process functional descriptions, control narratives, PFDs and P&IDs, and selection of instrumentation for various applications for the Great Bear Project.

Ensure that the engineering design meets project specifications, safety standards, and regulatory requirements.

Provide feedback and recommend modifications to optimize design efficiency and functionality.

Oversee key engineering deliverables of I&C consultants in design offices and work of contractors on-site.

Ensure consultants and contractors adhere to project timelines, budgets, and quality standards.

Coordinate with consultants and contractors to resolve any issues or challenges that arise during detailed design, construction, and commissioning.

Collaborate with cross-functional teams of consultants, contractors, vendors, and work closely with the Great Bear Project team to ensure quality engineering deliverables regarding safety in design, constructability and cost.

Conduct required inspections and audits of I&C design, manufacturing, and installations.

Ensure compliance with safety regulations and best practices.

Maintain detailed records of all I&C engineering activities.

Prepare and submit regular reports to lead engineers.

Document any design changes, modifications, or issues encountered.

Job Summary

The Open Pit Superintendent will be responsible for overseeing the safe, efficient, and cost-effective execution of all open pit mining activities, including drilling, blasting, loading, and hauling operations. This position provides leadership and direction to operational teams, ensuring production targets are achieved in alignment with short and long term mine plans, budget, and engineering standards. The Superintendent is accountable for the safety, performance, and development of the open pit team and for managing the area operating budget and resources to meet operational objectives.

Oversee and direct open pit mining operations, ensuring safe, efficient execution of drilling, blasting, loading, and hauling activities to achieve production targets.

Ensure effective coordination between Mining, Maintenance, Processing, and Technical Services teams to meet site objectives.

Oversee drill and blast and haulage activities to ensure plans are executed safely and in accordance with Kinross, Great Bear standards.

Mange the pit operation to ensure production targets are achieved and within expected ore grade targets and use all available tools to drive continuous improvement.

Develop medium to long term forecasting plans (people, equipment) to effectively execute operational targets.

Assist with the preparation of annual budgets and business plans and manage operational costs

Collaborate with Senior Leadership, Technical Services, Maintenance, and other support departments.

Coordinate workforce planning, training, and succession development.

Provide leadership, coaching, and mentorship to supervision and production crews, leading by example and visibly putting health and safety first to build a strong safety culture.

Work in a healthy work environment with full support, cooperation, and commitment to satisfy our operation’s goal of being accident-free.

Job Summary

The Process Control Engineer is responsible for developing, maintaining, and optimizing process control systems that support safe, reliable, and efficient mineral processing operations at the Round Mountain Gold Mine. This role focuses on improving plant stability, throughput, recovery, and equipment performance through effective control strategies, automation enhancements, and close collaboration with operations, metallurgy, and maintenance teams.

Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

Essential Functions

Process Control & Automation
•    Design, implement, maintain, and optimize control strategies for crushing, grinding, classification, leaching, adsorption, detoxification, and ancillary systems as applicable.
•    Configure, troubleshoot, and support plant control systems (e.g., DCS, PLCs, HMI/SCADA) to ensure high system availability and reliability.
•    Develop and tune regulatory, advanced, and model-based control loops to improve process stability and metallurgical performance.
•    Lead and support control system upgrades, logic changes, alarm management, and interface improvements in accordance with site change management procedures.
Operational Support
•    Partner with Operations and Metallurgy to identify process constraints and variability, and implement control solutions that improve throughput, recovery, and reagent efficiency.
•    Provide on-shift and off-shift technical support for control system issues impacting production or safety.
•    Analyze process data and trends to proactively identify opportunities for improvement and risk mitigation.
Maintenance & Reliability Interface
•    Work closely with the Process Maintenance Superintendent and maintenance teams to support instrumentation, control hardware, and network reliability.
•    Support preventative maintenance strategies, control system documentation, and lifecycle management of automation assets.
•    Assist with root cause analysis for process upsets and equipment or control-related failures.
Safety, Compliance & Standards
•    Promote a strong safety culture by ensuring control systems support safe operating limits and critical safeguards.
•    Participate in hazard analyses, management of change (MOC), and operational readiness reviews.
Projects & Continuous Improvement
•    Provide process control expertise for capital projects, plant modifications, and technology trials.
•    Develop functional specifications, FAT/SAT documentation, and commissioning plans for automation-related projects.
•    Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives focused on cost reduction, energy efficiency, and operational excellence.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

•    Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering, Automation, or a related discipline.
•    5–8 years of experience in process control or automation within mineral processing, mining, or heavy industrial environments.
•    Familiarity with CMMS 
•    Hands-on experience with DCS and/or PLC platforms commonly used in mining operations (e.g., Honeywell, ABB, Emerson, Rockwell).
•    Strong understanding of mineral processing unit operations and their control requirements.
•    Control loop tuning, alarm management, and control system troubleshooting.
•    Process data analysis and visualization tools (e.g., Wonderware, PI System or equivalent historians).
•    Instrumentation fundamentals, including flow, level, pressure, density, and analytical measurements.

•    Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.

The IT Specialist is a hands‑on, customer‑focused technologist who keeps Bald Mountain’s users productive and our site technology resilient. jobs.title: Superintendent, Site Services (Red Lake, ON, CA)
jobs.description:
The Great Bear project is a development-stage asset located in the renowned and prolific Red Lake mining district, and represents one of the most exciting recent gold discoveries globally.  The project has excellent potential to become a top-tier deposit that could support a large, long-life mine complex. Kinross’ comprehensive exploration and development program will aim to support the vision of a quality, high-grade, open-pit mine and a longer-term, sizeable underground mine.

Job Summary

As the Superintendent, Site Services for the Great Bear Project you will provide leadership, planning, and overall accountability for the safe, reliable, and cost-effective delivery of site services. The role leads the operation, maintenance, and repair oversight of surface infrastructure, facilities and utilities, logistics, yard operations, waste management, water treatment, and associated maintenance activities, and provides direction to the Supervisor, Site Services internal crews, and contractors. Until the start of main project construction, you will oversee the maintenance and repair of site infrastructure, utilities, facilities, and non-core operational assets following handover from Project, supporting underground development and exploration including the operation of the 13km Chukuni Pipeline, worker camp and associated effluent treatment system. Upon project transition into full operations, you will assume full accountability for non-core operational assets following handover from Project.

Key Responsibilities and Duties

Provide leadership, planning, and direction for site services team responsible for the operation and maintenance of the worker camp, yards, roads, utilities, logistics, site-wide waste management, and non-core infrastructure.

Develop and execute site services budgets, plans, preventative maintenance programs, and resource requirements in alignment with operational priorities. Support to the Projects team on an as-needed basis.

Establish and monitor service levels and key performance indicators for safety, environmental compliance, asset reliability, maintenance completion, cost, budget schedule; identify trends and implement corrective actions.

Provide oversight of contracts and contractors related to site services’ areas of responsibility.

Develop and implement contingency and business continuity planning for utility outages, equipment failures, severe weather, transportation disruptions, and other events that could affect site services.

Lead, coach, and hold accountable the Site Services Supervisor(s) and internal crews; establish clear roles, rotation handovers, staffing plans, training requirements, and performance expectations.

Participate in the development and execution of the Operational Readiness Plan for surface infrastructure, including maintenance strategies, procedures, staffing, training, spares, and service continuity.

Work in a healthy work environment with full support, cooperation, and commitment to satisfy our operation’s goal of being accident-free.

Support a work environment that is aligned with Kinross’ Safeground principles.

Comply with federal and provincial acts and regulations, and legal requirements.

Adhere to all relevant Great Bear policies and procedures.

Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

A minimum of 7–10 years of progressive experience in site services, facilities, infrastructure, maintenance, logistics, or related functions within mining, construction, or industrial environments, including 3-5 years in a supervisory or superintendent capacity.

Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and contractors in a remote operating environment, during the start up phase, is required. 

A technical diploma, trade certificate, or equivalent combination of education and experience in mining, mechanical systems, and/or facilities management is preferred.

Strong working knowledge of site services support equipment such as forklifts, skid steers, generators, etc.

Strong knowledge of carpentry, plumbing, electrical, and mechanical systems and maintenance best practices.

Knowledge of materials-handling practices, lifting and rigging requirements, and safe equipment operation.

Experience with contractor management and project execution in remote mining environments.

Ability to read, interpret, and apply operating manuals and procedures.

Benefits

At Kinross, Great Bear, we are committed to Putting People First by fostering employee growth and development, celebrating achievements, and rewarding team success. Benefits offered for this position include: 

Annual Fitness and Mental Health Reimbursement

Employee Share Purchase Plan, Registered Retirement Savings, and Registered Pension Plans

160 Hours of Paid Vacation

Employee Assistance Program

Employee Recognition Program

Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance

Life, Accidental Death & Dismemberment, and Disability Insurance

Training and Development Opportunities

Relocation assistance may be provided to eligible candidates on a case-by-case basis

Work Conditions

This position is based in Red Lake, Ontario. Local candidates, or those willing to relocate, with relocation assistance, will be given priority for this position. The schedule for this position is 14X14, 12 hour days. 

Compensation and Total Rewards

The base salary for the Superintendent, Site Services is $140,000.00 to $170,000.00 + Short Term Incentive, + Long Term Incentive, + Group Benefit Coverage. 

The hiring range reflects our targeted compensation framework for the role. The actual offer will be determined through a comprehensive evaluation of each candidate's experience, capabilities, and potential impact, along with consideration of internal equity, team structure, and benchmark market data for similar positions. Job Summary

Kinross Round Mountain is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable and safe mining practices. We are committed to innovation and excellence in all our operations. Join our team to contribute to challenging and rewarding projects in a dynamic and supportive environment. Round Mountain is renowned as one of the most geotechnically challenging mines in Nevada.

Our Round Mountain Technical Services team is seeking a Underground Surveyor Supervisor to lead the Underground Survey group for the Underground Mine at Round Mountain Gold Mine. Reporting to the UG Chief Mine Engineer, you will lead the underground survey department, manage survey standards and quality control, and provide accurate, timely spatial data to engineering, geology, and operations. This role will ensure that all underground workings, long-hole stopes, and infrastructure are surveyed, mapped, and reported to support safe and efficient mining. The underground is currently in its early development stages and now transitioning from exploration development to capital development. This is a great opportunity for a motivated individual to build the foundation for the underground survey group, standards, and procedures that will be used for the life of mine.  

Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

Essential Functions

•  Survey Leadership and Team Management
Lead, train, and develop the underground survey team, ensuring consistent technical performance and adherence to best practices. Assign daily and weekly survey tasks aligned with mine planning and production priorities. Maintain a culture of safety, accuracy, and continuous improvement within the survey group.
•  Underground Surveying and Data Collection
Establish and maintain underground survey control networks, including primary and secondary control points. Perform development surveys, including heading markups, line and grade, and breakthrough checks. Conduct production surveys for long hole stopes, including collaring, toe checks, and cavity monitoring. Capture as built data for development, infrastructure, and backfill operations.
•  Long-hole Stoping Support
Provide precise drill markups for long hole production drilling. Verify stope boundaries, slot raises, and breakthrough locations to minimize dilution and ensure compliance with design. Survey underground backfill boundaries to support geotechnical and engineering QA/QC.
•  Data Management and Reporting
Maintain accurate survey databases, digital models, and spatial records. Deliver timely updates to mine engineering, geology, and operations, including 3D models, maps, and progress reports. Support reconciliation of planned vs. actual development and stope performance on a regular cadence as needed (daily, weekly, monthly)
•  Technology, Equipment, and Quality Control
Oversee maintenance, calibration, and proper use of survey instruments (total stations, scanners, LiDAR, GPS for surface tie ins). Implement QA/QC procedures for all survey data and deliverables. Evaluate and adopt new survey technologies to improve accuracy and efficiency.

•  Safety, Compliance, and Regulatory Requirements
Ensure all survey activities comply with MSHA regulations and site safety standards. Participate in underground inspections, hazard identification, and risk assessments. Support environmental and operational compliance through accurate spatial documentation.

•    Degree or diploma in Surveying, Geomatics, Mining Engineering Technology, or related field (preferred)

Job Summary

Ensure supervision excellence for the Projects Department while continuously aligning daily functions to reflect Kinross’ values.  This position is a full-time position to supervise ongoing projects both capital and non-capital assigned by the Projects Superintendent projects for Kinross Nevada, while continuously aligning daily functions to reflect Kinross’ values. 

Essential Functions

1.  Support Projects and Operational groups at Round Mountain as assigned.
2.  Act as liaison between stakeholders and business partners on-site to meet engineering specs. and supervision requirements set by RMGC.
3.  Write and review SOW’s when required for each project.  
4.  Review bids and evaluate with the stakeholders which proposal to recommended to Supply Chain.
5.  Write PTW (Permit to Work) for departments and business partners when needed.

12.  Perform other related functions as assigned by Superintendent.
13.  Consistently exercise discretion and judgment in job performance.
14.  Maintaining a high level of confidentiality in the workplace and off work is crucial for protecting sensitive information, ensuring trust, and adhering to legal and ethical standards.

1.  Must be a self-starter.
2.  Must be willing to devote the time required to complete capital projects and be on call during off time if needed.
3.  Knowledge of pump and piping systems, structural design, conveyor systems, electrical and instrumentation and control is preferred.
4.  Knowledge of project structure and supervision is preferred.
5.  The ability to effectively manage the development of all projects assigned.
6.  A minimum of five years’ experience working in the mining or construction industry.
7.  Strong verbal, written, analytical and persuasive skills and the ability to interact effectively with all levels of employees and management.
8.  Must be able to balance resource allocations with changing priorities as required.

10.  Must be a salaried person and have a minimum of 5 years supervisory experience required.

jobs.description:

Job Summary

The Mine Engineer I reports to the Senior Mine Engineer and is responsible for carrying out a full range of engineering functions including, but not limited to: mine planning, leach stacking plans, drill pattern design, drill and blast scheduling, blast pattern design, pit designs, stockpile, road and dump designs, mine analysis and production reporting. Will have direct involvement and communication with staff from other departments (Geology, Geotechnics, Maintenance and Operations).
Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

Essential Functions

1.  Develop and communicate engineering plans, technical reports and presentations, sequences, dumping priorities, etc. to Mine Operations and other stakeholders on site and ensure plans are carried out safely and efficiently 
2.  Leading pit tour with mine operations, supporting mine operations on the daily production meeting.
3.  Working on optimizing and improving the short-range planning processes
4.  Develop weekly mine plan, weekly mill feed strategy and perform a weekly mine plan adherence.  
5.  Drill and Blast Planning and Scheduling 
6.  Utilize geological data, mine plans and survey information to develop blast designs and shot timing, and release patterns as required for execution.
7.  Consult and develop a close working relationship with the Geotechnical Engineer in order to optimize pit wall stability.
8.  Perform accurate Drill/Blast pattern design duties on time - Preparation and Implementation of a Weekly Drill and Blast Plan.
9.  Perform pit design, dump design and infrastructure/road design.
10.  Identify risks (production and mine movement, equipment priorities, geotech, dewatering, grade, manpower, etc.) and opportunities that may impact the mine plans.
11.  Ensure information flow and buy-in to the mine plan process from various departments (load and haul, drill and blast, processing, etc).
12.  Collect and interpret technical data such as blast-induced vibration and utilize findings to inform pattern design decisions and improvements, with specific focus on high-risk sectors of the open pit.
13.  Safety Performance & Record, perform field engagement and risk identifications.
14.  Ensure drill & blast planning complies with applicable safety regulations, environmental standards, standard operating procedures and company best practices.
15.  Promote and engage strongly with a pro-active safety culture.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

1.  Bachelor’s degree in Mining Engineering or similar field is required.
2.  1-5 years of planning and/or drill & blast experience in hard-rock, open pit mine operations is strongly preferred.
3.  Proficiency with mining software packages (Deswik, AutoCAD, Vulcan, MineSite) is strongly preferred.
4.  Working knowledge of mine operations and drill & blast principles.
5.  Comfortable working collaboratively in a team environment.
6.  Strong engagement with technical details, self-motivated to learn and continuously improve our mine planning and drill & blast practices.
7.  Must be presently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. 
8.  Valid driver’s license is required.

Health, Safety, and Environmental Requirements

•    Has a strong commitment to safe working practices. 
•    Wears Personal Protective Equipment at all times while in the production environment. 
•    Is alert and observes, corrects, and reports unsafe conditions. 
•    Follows operating procedures and complies with all regulatory requirements.

Job Summary

The Senior Mine Engineer (Long Range) is responsible for developing, maintaining, and optimizing the Life of Mine (LOM) plans and designs for Kinross Nevada open-pit operations. This role ensures long-term strategic plans are economically optimized, safe, and compliant with geotechnical and environmental standards. They work closely with technical services, geology, and site management to maximize shareholder value and operational performance.

Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

1.    Strategic Mine Planning: Run pit optimizations and support mineral inventory reporting requirements, optimize mine plans, fleet sizing studies, create stack plans, and technical studies focused on asset optimization.
2.    Design And Modelling: Create open pits, waste rock dumps, haul roads and stormwater drainages. Able to check block models using drill data, run statistics and create scripts preferred.
3.    Scheduling and Economic Analysis: Integrates short-term plans into long-term, and life-of-mine plans. Perform excel level economic analysis. Support feasibility studies (NI 43-101) as required.
4.    Reconciliation and Compliance: Analyzes and interprets mine plans to ensure alignment with financial, environmental and operational objectives. Perform reconciliation of actuals vs. planned production, updating plans to reflect reality while maximizing NPV.
5.    Collaboration: Work with short range planners, environmental, exploration, metallurgy, geotech, maintenance, and leadership teams to ensure long term plans are technically sound.
6.    Innovation: Researches information to support decision-making and improve processes, technologies or methodologies.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

1.    B.S. Degree in Mining or related discipline.
2.    5 Years of experience in surface mining preferred.
3.    Comprehensive knowledge of the principles and concepts of open pit mining engineering.

6.    Proficiency in MS Office suite of software (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).

Join our team to contribute to challenging and rewarding projects in a dynamic and supportive environment. Round Mountain is renowned as one of the most geotechnically challenging mines in Nevada.

Our Round Mountain Technical Services team is seeking an experienced Chief Underground Mining Engineer to lead the underground tech services group comprising of mine engineers, planners, surveyors, ventilation engineers, and technical technicians for the Underground Mine at Round Mountain Gold Mine. Reporting to the UG Technical Services Manager, you will ensure that the mine’s long-hope stoping mining method is designed, scheduled, and executed safely and profitably. This role will also act as the primary technical liaison between operations, geology, and management. The underground is currently in its early development stages and now transitioning from exploration development to capital development. This is a great opportunity for a motivated individual to build the foundation for the underground mining engineering group, standards, and procedures that will be used for the life of mine.  

Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

Essential Functions

• Mine Planning & Design
Develop and oversee short , mid , and long range mine plans for a long hole stoping operation using paste backfill and cemented rockfill. Approve stope designs, drill patterns, sequencing, and ground support strategies. Ensure backfill requirements (strength, timing, curing windows) are integrated into the mine schedule. Optimize stope sequencing to balance geotechnical stability, ventilation constraints, and production targets
• Technical Leadership & Team Management
Lead, mentor, and develop mine engineers, surveyors, and technical staff. Foster a collaborative environment between engineering and operations, emphasizing problem solving and continuous improvement. Set technical standards, review engineering work, and ensure quality control across all engineering deliverables.
• Operational Support
Provide real time technical guidance to underground operations, including drilling, blasting, backfilling, and ground support installation. Troubleshoot stope performance issues (dilution, overbreak, paste delivery, drilling accuracy). Coordinate with maintenance, backfill plant personnel, and production supervisors to ensure alignment with engineering plans
• Safety, Regulatory, and Environmental Compliance
Ensure all engineering designs comply with MSHA regulations and Nevada state mining requirements. Support and reinforce site Health & Safety Management Systems and environmental compliance programs. Lead risk assessments for new stopes, mining methods, or ground conditions.
• Backfill & Geotechnical Integration
Work closely with geotechnical engineers to ensure stope stability, pillar design, and sequencing meet safety and production needs. Oversee paste backfill and CRF design parameters, QA/QC, and scheduling to maintain mine stability and minimize dilution.

• Budgeting & Project Management
Manage engineering department budgets, staffing, and capital project planning. Lead or support underground capital projects (ventilation upgrades, dewatering systems, new development headings, backfill plant improvements). Evaluate and justify new technologies, equipment, or software to improve efficiency.
• Data Management & Reporting
Oversee production reporting, stope reconciliation, and variance analysis. Ensure accurate survey control, mine modeling, and engineering databases. Present engineering updates to senior leadership and contribute to life of mine planning.

jobs.title: Leach General Supervisor (Round Mountain, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Round Mountain is an open-pit mine located in Nevada, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world. The mine uses conventional open-pit mining methods and processes ore by mill and heap leach. Kinross began operating the mine in 2003, and it has since become a continuous improvement leader in the Company’s portfolio. Round Mountain poured its 15 millionth ounce in 2018. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Summary

The Processing General Supervisor is responsible for leading safe, reliable, and efficient day-to-day processing operations to achieve production, recovery, and cost objectives. Reporting to the Processing Superintendent, this role provides operational leadership across ore processing activities, coordinates closely with maintenance, mining, technical services, and metallurgy, and develops high-performing teams through clear expectations, coaching, and accountability. The successful candidate will bring strong processing knowledge, sound operational judgment, and a visible commitment to safety, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.

Essential Functions

•  Lead by example and maintain a visible, proactive safety culture that supports safe production and environmental stewardship.
•  Ensure compliance with company standards, operating procedures, and applicable federal, state, and site-specific regulations.
•  Conduct effective safety meetings, field interactions, inspections, and follow-up actions to identify and address hazards promptly.
•  Hold crews, contractors, and peers accountable to safe work practices, operating discipline, and respectful workplace expectations.
•  Lead, coach, and develop supervisors to build a capable, engaged, and high-performing processing team.
•  Set clear expectations, monitor performance, provide timely feedback, and support employee development and succession planning.
•  Drive staffing activities as needed, including interviewing, selection input, onboarding, and task training.
•  Organize work priorities and deploy labor and resources effectively to meet operating requirements across the shift.
•  Promote a respectful, collaborative work environment grounded in accountability, communication, and teamwork.
•  Oversee daily operation of assigned processing areas to meet production and recovery targets safely and efficiently.
•  Coordinate with mining, maintenance, metallurgy, and technical services to align priorities, optimize plant performance, and support the daily operating plan.
•  Monitor process conditions, equipment availability, operational KPIs, and recovery/efficiency trends; respond quickly to deviations and emerging risks.
•  Troubleshoot operational issues, implement corrective actions, and support continuous improvement initiatives that improve stability, productivity, and cost performance.
•  Ensure operating procedures are followed consistently and that process equipment is utilized effectively and maintained in coordination with maintenance teams.
•  Use sound judgment and discretion in operational decision-making while balancing safety, people, equipment, and production priorities.
•  Complete and verify accurate production, shift, maintenance, training, and safety documentation in a timely manner.
•  Prepare and communicate operational updates, performance results, key risks, and improvement opportunities to site leadership.
•  Support development, revision, and implementation of standard operating procedures, training materials, and operating standards.
•  Identify opportunities to improve systems, workflows, and operating practices that strengthen reliability, compliance, and team effectiveness.
•  Other duties as assigned. 

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

•  Minimum five (5) years of processing and/or ore processing operations experience
•  Minimum five (5) years in a demonstrated leadership in a supervisory capacity.
•  High school diploma or GED required; additional technical training in mineral processing, metallurgy, mechanical systems, or a related field is preferred.
•  Demonstrated ability to lead crews, coordinate work activities, and drive safe, reliable production in a fast-paced mining environment.
•  Strong communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to work effectively across all levels of the organization and apply policies fairly and consistently required.
•  Ability to coach, develop, and hold employees accountable while maintaining a respectful and collaborative team environment.
•  Experience with plant reporting systems, Microsoft Office, and operational business systems; familiarity with JDE or similar CMMS is preferred.
•  Strong safety record and demonstrated commitment to environmental compliance, operating discipline, and continuous improvement.
•  Must be at least 18 years of age and authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis.
•  Valid driver’s license required.

Health, Safety, and Environmental Requirements

•  Adheres to all safety and environmental considerations.
•  Have a strong commitment to safe working practices. 
•  Wears personal protective equipment at all times while in the production environment. 
•  Is alert and observes, corrects, and reports unsafe conditions. 
•  Follows operating procedures and complies with all regulatory requirements. 

Kinross Competencies

•  Strategic Effectiveness
Developing and communicating rigorous and creative business strategies that drive sustainable value.
•  External Engagement
Understanding and building relationships with external parties that strengthen and sustain competitive advantage.
•  Business Focus
Applying commercial rigor and discipline to all business decisions and customer relationships.
•  Living the Kinross Values
Aligning

jobs.description:
Bald Mountain is an open-pit mine with a large estimated mineral resource in the largest private mining land package in the U.S. The mine is located in White Pine County, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world, along the southern extension of the prolific Carlin trend. This role demands advanced expertise in various mechanical systems, including braking, steering, and suspension, as well as proficiency in electronic engine controls and hydraulic systems. The ability to read and interpret hydraulic and

electrical schematics is crucial for effective troubleshooting and maintenance tasks. Proficiency with Cat SIS, Cat ET, and Cummins InSite are helpful.

While this role ideally suits an experienced mechanic, we welcome applicants with strong mechanical aptitude and  willingness to further develop skill sets.

The position requires a strong understanding of mechanical systems and safety practices while ensuring minimal downtime for equipment and compliance with Kinross' safety and operational standards.

This position follows a rotating 5/4 schedule, alternating between day and night shifts. Flexibility to work weekends, holidays, and overtime as needed is required.

jobs.title: Supervisor(a) Senior de Operaciones Mineroducto
jobs.description:
Misión del Puesto

Supervisar las actividades de Despacho de Concentrado, maximizando la capacidad de bombeo dentro de los parámetros de diseño asegurando una operación confiable y segura del Mineroducto. Coordinar con las diferentes guardias del Mineroducto para asegurar que se ejecuten las buenas prácticas de operación acorde a las políticas de la empresa y de los requerimientos de sus Sistemas de Gestión.

Responsabilidades y Actividades Principales

Planificar, coordinar y controlar la operación de transporte de concentrados a través del Mineroducto, integrando los planes de producción, requerimientos de embarque, capacidades de bombeo y almacenamiento y condiciones operativas del sistema, a fin de asegurar el cumplimiento del programa de transporte y contribuir a la continuidad del proceso productivo.

Definir y coordinar las condiciones operativas requeridas para las intervenciones programadas y no programadas del Mineroducto, articulando con Mantenimiento los plazos de intervención y supervisando las operaciones de drenaje, llenado y restitución del sistema, a fin de minimizar los tiempos de indisponibilidad y asegurar el restablecimiento seguro y oportuno de la operación.

Evaluar y optimizar las condiciones de transporte hidráulico de concentrados, integrando información operacional, análisis estadísticos y comportamiento reológico de las pulpas, a fin de maximizar la capacidad de bombeo y eficiencia del sistema, optimizando el consumo energético y la utilización de la infraestructura disponible.

Controlar el desempeño operacional del Mineroducto y determinar acciones ante desviaciones de sus parámetros y límites de diseño, analizando tendencias e indicadores críticos de presión, flujo, densidad y comportamiento hidráulico, a fin de prevenir eventos operacionales y mantener la operación dentro de condiciones seguras, estables y confiables.

Desarrollar, actualizar y liderar la implementación de los planes de contingencia operativa del Mineroducto, evaluando escenarios de riesgo y determinando las acciones operacionales correspondientes ante emergencias o condiciones no rutinarias, a fin de controlar sus consecuencias, proteger a las personas y el medio ambiente y facilitar la recuperación segura de la operación.

Elaborar y controlar el presupuesto OPEX y CAPEX correspondiente a las actividades bajo su responsabilidad, realizando seguimiento a su ejecución, analizando desviaciones y proponiendo acciones de optimización, a fin de asegurar el uso eficiente de los recursos económicos y el cumplimiento de los planes operativos.

jobs.description:
Misión del Puesto

Gestionar la planificación, consolidación, seguimiento y control del presupuesto operativo (OPEX) y de capital (CAPEX) de las áreas asignadas de la Vicepresidencia de Operaciones, mediante el análisis y generación de información financiera oportuna y confiable, con el propósito de contribuir a la toma de decisiones y al uso eficiente de los recursos, acorde a las políticas de la empresa y de los requerimientos de sus sistemas de gestión.

Responsabilidades y Actividades Principales

Consolidar el presupuesto anual, el Plan de Cinco Años (5YP) y el Life of Mine (LOM) de OPEX y CAPEX de las áreas asignadas de la Vicepresidencia de Operaciones, para asegurar la disponibilidad de información precisa que respalde la formulación presupuestal liderada por la Superintendencia.

Controlar el desempeño presupuestal de costos y proyectos de las áreas asignadas, para identificar oportunamente desviaciones y facilitar la implementación de acciones correctivas que fortalezcan la disciplina operativa y financiera.

Realizar el seguimiento de la ejecucion del proceso de cierre mensual de OPEX y CAPEX en coordinación con las gerencias de la VPO y ser el nexo entre con el área de Finanzas, para garantizar la confiabilidad, oportunidad e integridad de la información operativa, económica y financiera.

Identificar, evaluar y hacer seguimiento de las iniciativas de optimización y ahorro de costos, en coordinación con las gerencias de la VPO, para contribuir a la eficiencia operativa y la generación de valor para el negocio.

Consolidar los pronósticos (Forecast) de OPEX y CAPEX, así como el análisis de variaciones respecto al presupuesto y proyecciones previas, para facilitar la toma de decisiones y anticipar impactos económicos en la operación.

Brindar asesoramiento en materia de costos, proyectos y presupuestos de las gerencias de la VPO, para facilitar una gestión estandarizada y la toma de decisiones de las áreas usuarias.

Evaluar y monitorear las iniciativas relacionadas al desarrollo de la innovación y nuevas tecnologías costos y presupuestos, para promover la mejora continua, la eficiencia de los procesos y la generación de valor para el negocio.

Elaborar dashboards y analizar los indicadores de gestión, costos unitarios y las principales desviaciones presupuestales y de ejecucion con herramientas, aplicaciones y analitica, para identificar oportunidades de mejora y fortalecer la eficiencia en el uso de los recursos.

Participar en la planificación de las operaciones de recepción, almacenamiento y transporte de concentrados a través del Mineroducto, considerando los planes de producción, requerimientos de embarque, capacidad de bombeo y almacenamiento y condiciones operativas del sistema, a fin de asegurar el cumplimiento del programa de transporte y la continuidad de las operaciones.

Coordinar con Mantenimiento las intervenciones programadas y no programadas del Mineroducto, evaluando las condiciones operativas y plazos disponibles para la ejecución de los trabajos, a fin de minimizar los tiempos de detención y su impacto en el programa de transporte de concentrados.

Supervisar la operación del Mineroducto dentro de los parámetros y límites establecidos de diseño, monitoreando tendencias e indicadores críticos de presión, flujo, densidad y demás variables operativas, a fin de identificar oportunamente desviaciones y prevenir eventos que puedan afectar la seguridad, integridad y continuidad del sistema.

jobs.title: Supervisor Maintenance, Facilities
jobs.description:
Elk Valley Resources (EVR) operates four steelmaking coal mines that employ over 5,000 people in the Elk Valley of British Columbia. We are committed to responsible resource development, environmental performance and building strong partnerships with communities and Indigenous Peoples.

EVR is proud to be part of the Glencore Group, contributing to a global portfolio of operations with a history that dates back more than 100 years in Canada

.

Are you looking for a new career opportunity? Join our team.

Application Deadline: October 6, 2026

What we offer:

At EVR, we're dedicated to supporting our workforce on their unique career journeys.

EVR recognizes our employees' skills, competencies, and performance and offers opportunities with competitive compensation and benefits. We also aim to promote employee health and wellness and provide opportunities for professional development.

We believe in the power of diversity and strive each day to create a workplace where each individual is valued and respected for their contributions.

We also believe that our employees are the reason we are accomplishing great things and are committed to supporting them through our many different programs.

About the role:

Reporting to the Superintendent, Maintenance, the Supervisor Maintenance, Facilities will be responsible for supporting management and maintenance of site facilities at Elkview Operations. The Supervisor will have a compliment of labourers and tradespeople, and be responsible for supervision of contractors as required, ensuring contractor adherence to the BC Mines Code and EVR’s Health and Safety policies and procedures, and conducting regular job site inspections and audits.

To be successful, we are looking for someone with excellent organizational, interpersonal and communication skills, who can coordinate the efforts of others to accomplish objectives. Someone who will thrive in a fast-paced environment with minimal direction but also works well collaborating with a team. Strong problem- solving, multi-tasking and decision-making abilities are vital in this role.

Join us in the breathtaking Elk Valley of British Columbia. Here you will find outdoor adventure at your fingertips. Whether it's biking and skiing, or the laid-back atmosphere of fishing and hiking, there is something for everyone! Working a shift schedule of 4x4 steady days, come experience what work life balance is all about!

Two Annual Bonus Plans

Comprehensive Benefits Plan

Retirement Package

Health Lifestyle Account

Relocation Assistance

Participate in and adhere to health and safety programs and policies

Advise the troubleshooting of equipment failures to determine root cause and initiate appropriate remedial action

Coordinate quality maintenance and repair of assets to improve availability and reliability for production

Handle daily and weekly work schedules to ensure work is completed on time and on budget

Supervise and improve employee work performance and efficiency, ensuring quality standards

Assist in sourcing and requisitioning supplies, equipment, and services within budgeted guidelines

Ensure repair history is accurately detailed as work is performed

Maintain vacation schedules using Vacation Allotment guidelines, recommending and approving overtime work

Recommend contractor needs based on load and supervise contractors

Lead unionized hourly workers, contractors and collaborate closely with other external partners

Work with all partners within Elkview Operations, to develop and implement the overall maintenance strategy for the site

Track and report Key Performance Indicators of our maintenance processes and systems

Work to identify maintenance improvement opportunities and identifying maintenance processes which are either missing or are not being utilized

Coordinate the development and sharing of ‘Best Practice’ templates for work planning, scheduling and execution

High school diploma and Journeyperson’s ticket, related technical diploma or Engineering degree, or equivalent combination of education and experience

Excellent digital literacy in Microsoft Office Suite® particularly in Excel, Outlook, and Word

Experience in execution, planning and scheduling maintenance activities

Supervisory or team leading experience would be considered an asset

Technical understanding of equipment maintenance and maintenance strategies and their implementation

Experience with materials acquisition, planning, and scheduling

Experience with budgeting and accrual processes

Experience with digital systems and real time monitoring equipment

Familiar with the regulatory environment associated with industrial maintenance processes, and systems

BC Mine Supervisor Certificate and Mine Rescue certification is an asset, or willingness to acquire

Knowledge of BC’s Health, Safety and Reclamation Code is an asset

Valid Class 5 Driver’s License or equivalent

jobs.title: Ingeniero(a) de Excelencia Operacional
jobs.description:
Misión del Puesto

Gestionar e implementar iniciativas de mejora continua mediante el análisis y optimización de procesos, la aplicación de metodologías y el desarrollo de capacidades organizacionales, para mejorar el desempeño operacional, reducir la variabilidad operacional, incrementar la productividad y capturar valor sostenible para Antamina, acorde a las políticas de la empresa y de los requerimientos de sus sistemas de gestión.

Responsabilidades y Actividades Principales

Gestionar el portafolio de iniciativas de Full Potential (enfocadas a aumentar la productividad y optimización de costos), identificando, priorizando e identificando oportunidades de generación de valor para maximizar el desempeño operativo y financiero de la Vicepresidencia de Operaciones.

Brindar soporte metodológico a líderes y equipos operativos en la aplicación de metodologías y herramientas de mejora continua , resolución de problemas y gestión del cambio, con el propósito de fortalecer sus capacidades y asegurar la adopción y sostenibilidad de las mejoras implementadas.

Analizar el desempeño de los procesos operacionales mediante indicadores, tendencias y desviaciones respecto de metas y estándares, con el propósito de generar información para la toma de decisiones e identificar brechas que requieran acciones de mejora.

Diseñar e implementar el modelo de excelencia operacional de la Vicepresidencia de Operaciones, integrando la gestión del desempeño, la estabilización y mejora continua de los procesos para asegurar la alineación entre los objetivos estratégicos, la ejecución de los procesos y los resultados esperados.

Facilitar diagnósticos y análisis de causa raíz de procesos críticos, identificando desperdicios, cuellos de botella y oportunidades de optimización para incrementar la productividad y eficiencia operacional.

Desarrollar y dar seguimiento a los casos de negocio de las iniciativas de mejora e iniciativas estratégicas, validando beneficios y monitoreando resultados para asegurar el cumplimiento acorde al alcance de cada iniciativa.

Liderar la implementación y  la estandarización de los trabajos de las áreas operativas y de mantenimiento para reducir la variabilidad operacional y promover la mejora continua de los procesos.

Promover espacios de colaboración transversal, facilitando el alineamiento entre áreas operativas y de soporte para acelerar la implementación de mejoras y la captura de beneficios.

Cumplir las normas y procedimientos de Seguridad Industrial a fin de proteger la vida y salud de las personas, prevenir accidentes graves y garantizar operaciones seguras y sostenibles.

Cumplir con otras responsabilidades delegadas por su supervisión directa ligadas a su posición que aseguren la sostenibilidad del negocio.    

Formación Requerida

Bachiller en Ingeniería Industrial, Minas, Metalurgia, Mecánica, Sistemas o carreras afines.

Otros Estudios

Indispensable contar con Certificación Lean Six Sigma Green Belt o Black Belt.

Deseable especialización en Excelencia Operacional, Lean Management, Gestión de Proyectos, metodologías Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, SMED o Gestión del Cambio.

Experiencia Previa

Mínimo 4 años de experiencia en operaciones mineras o industrias de procesos.

Mínimo 2 años de experiencia en roles similares en Mejora Continua, Excelencia Operacional, Business Improvement o Productividad en el sector minero.

Experiencia comprobada liderando proyectos de mejora y generación de valor.

Conocimientos Informáticos

Microsoft office: Intermedio

Software de análisis estadístico: Intermedio

Programación (deseable): Básico

Power BI (deseable): Intermedio

PIPware, Wave (deseable): Básico  

Idiomas

Inglés (deseable): Intermedio

Gerencia: Gestión y Excelencia Operacional

Superintendencia: Excelencia Operacional

Reporta a: Superintendente de Excelencia Operacional

jobs.description: ¡SÉ PARTE DE KOMATSU - MITSUI!Somos una empresa transnacional líder en el sector industrial, comprometida con el progreso y la innovación en uno de los sectores clave de nuestro país. Inspeccionar visualmente las soldaduras y reparaciones ejecutadas, identificando desviaciones y efectuando las correcciones requeridas conforme a los criterios de aceptación aplicables.- Monitorear permanentemente las condiciones de seguridad asociadas a los trabajos en caliente mediante la identificación de fuentes de ignición, materiales combustibles y riesgos potenciales, utilizando equipos de respuesta inicial cuando corresponda. ¿Qué te hace único?Educación: Egresado de carrera técnica relacionada con soldadura, mecánica de producción, construcciones metálicas o afinesExperiencia de mínimo uno (1) año de experiencia en un puesto de trabajo similar, en empresas del sector y/o afines (reparación estructural pesada minera y control de trabajos en caliente).Homologación 2G.Certificación/Capacitación como Vigía de Fuego (deseable). Nuestro proceso de selección está basado en la búsqueda de talento, sin importar origen étnico, sexo, edad, discapacidad, orientación sexual o cualquier otra condición personal.¡Forma parte de un equipo que desarrolla tu talento y transforma tu futuro!

Anglo American, en sociedad con la Corporación Mitsubishi, está desarrollando la operación minera Quellaveco, uno de los yacimientos de cobre más grandes del mundo, localizado en la región de Moquegua, al sur del Perú.

En Anglo American nos encontramos en búsqueda de un Oficial de Reparo.

RESPONSABILIDADES:

Es responsable de soportar el cumplimiento de los Planes de Reparación de los componentes y repuestos, a través del seguimiento y evaluación del cumplimiento de los requisitos técnicos y de servicio acordados con las áreas de mantenimiento y operaciones.

Esta posición se encargará de analizar el trabajo efectivo de las labores de reparación considerando los aspectos de seguridad, trazabilidad y recuperación eficiente de los componentes a fin de garantizar la continuidad operativa d ellos mismos.

El oficial será responsable de la gestión interna en SAP vinculada al registro de información, reportabilidad y seguimiento del cumplimiento de los términos y condiciones de las reparaciones a lo largo del ciclo de vida de los componentes.

FUNCIONES PRINCIPALES:

Asegurar la correcta ejecución y cumplimiento de los procedimientos de Almacenes en concordancia a los estándares SSOMA y exigencia gubernamental de la Normativa Peruana.

Liderar la seguridad de las personas dentro de las labores de almacenamiento y reparación, persiguiendo el cuidado del medio ambiente y comunidades.

Asegurar la trazabilidad y recuperación eficiente de los repuestos a fin de mantener la continuidad operativa en el mantenimiento, mediante un análisis directo en el ciclo de vida del componente o repuesto.

Ejecutar seguimiento a los procesos de envío y retorno de los componentes reparables en los talleres internos o externos establecidos por AA.

Ejecutar los conteos cíclicos en el inventario de los componentes reparables, así como asegurar su trazabilidad en el sistema ERP definido por AA.

Brindar soporte a la supervisión de reparables en el control documentario y registro de los informes técnicos de reparación acorde al ciclo de vida del componente.

Brindar análisis y reportabilidad de los indicadores de performance establecidos para optimizar los procesos de reparación de componentes, utilizando los sistemas de AA.

Coordinar la implementación de mejoras en el ERP de AA, a fin de brindar soporte al equipo de reparables.

Propiciar reuniones con las áreas de mantenimiento de AA a fin de asegurar que el proceso cumpla con todos los requisitos exigidos por el Modelo Operativo de AA.

Generar valor en los procesos de reparaciones y almacenes, a través de la eliminación de mudas y mejora continua a través de la aplicación de metodologías ágiles, 5S, lean supply.

Ejercer control de los materiales e insumos de tipo Material Peligroso, Insumo Químico Fiscalizado requerido en los procesos de gestión de reparaciones.

Conocimiento en gestión de componentes reparables en sectores como proyectos, minería, construcción, energía, hidrocarburos o gas.

jobs.title: Supervisor de Operaciones Mineras - Quiruvilca
jobs.description:
En nuestra empresa creemos que el talento crece cuando encuentra retos que lo desafían y oportunidades para hacer que las cosas sucedan. Por inicio de actividades en nuestra operación con Boroo, queremos sumar a un(a) Supervisor Operativo para liderar en campo las actividades de transporte y descarga en Quiruvilca, La Libertad.
Buscamos una persona con liderazgo, criterio operativo y capacidad de respuesta, que se desenvuelva bien en campo, movilice equipos y tome decisiones oportunas para asegurar una operación segura y eficiente.
El reto
Supervisar y coordinar las actividades de transporte y descarga, asegurando la continuidad de la operación, el cumplimiento de los programas de trabajo y el uso eficiente de personas y equipos, bajo los estándares de seguridad, calidad y medio ambiente.
Principales desafíos
Liderar al personal operativo, conductores y operadores, organizando las actividades y asegurando el cumplimiento de objetivos.
Supervisar las actividades de transporte y descarga, controlando tiempos, recursos y continuidad operativa.
Realizar seguimiento a las unidades en tránsito y coordinar mantenimientos preventivos y correctivos.
Monitorear productividad e indicadores operativos, identificando desviaciones y tomando acciones oportunas.
Verificar IPERC, checklists y procedimientos de trabajo seguro, asegurando condiciones adecuadas en campo.
Coordinar con las áreas involucradas y elaborar reportes de avance y resultados de la operación.
Capacitar y acompañar al equipo, fortaleciendo el desempeño y la cultura de seguridad.
¿Qué buscamos?
Titulado(a) en Ingeniería Química, Metalúrgica, Industrial, Minas o carreras afines.
Mínimo 2 años de experiencia como Supervisor de Producción, Supervisor Operativo o posiciones similares en operaciones mineras.
Experiencia liderando personal operativo (mínimo 10 personas).
Experiencia o conocimiento en transporte, descarga y seguimiento de equipos/unidades.
Licencia de conducir A2A o A2B con mínimo 2 años de antigüedad.
Conocimientos de IPERC y seguridad en campo.
Manejo de MS Office a nivel intermedio.
Deseable formación en planeamiento, control de producción y manejo de personal.
Condiciones
Ubicación: Lagunas Norte Quiruvilca, La Libertad.
Modalidad: 100 % presencial en unidad.
Régimen: 14x7.
Horario: Turnos rotativos; 1 semana de día (7:00 a. m. 7:00 p. m.) y 1 semana de noche (7:00 p. m. 7:00 a. m.)
¿Qué ofrecemos?
Ingreso a planilla con los beneficios correspondientes.
Alojamiento, alimentación y movilidad durante la operación.
Salario acorde al mercado.
La oportunidad de incorporarte al inicio de una nueva operación con Boroo, asumiendo liderazgo directo en campo y contribuyendo desde el inicio a consolidar una operación segura y eficiente.
· En nuestra empresa promovemos la inclusión laboral y la igualdad de oportunidades. Esta convocatoria está abierta a personas con discapacidad, según la Ley N.° 29973.-Requerimientos- Educación mínima: Universitario
3 años de experiencia
Edad: entre 23 y 45 años
Licencias de conducir: A-II-A ,A-II-B
Disponibilidad de viajar: Si
Disponibilidad de cambio de residencia: Si

jobs.description: En Manpower Perú buscamos al mejor talento para asumir el reto como Gestor de Soporte en Ingeniería (Precomisionado & QA) de Soporte en Electromecánico o Mecánico / Régimen 4x3 para nuestro cliente del sector Minero en la ciudad de Cajamarca. ¡La oportunidad de tener un futuro mejor está aquí!Funciones: Brindar soporte técnico especializado en la gestión de pruebas preoperacionales y actividades de aseguramiento de calidad, aplicando estándares técnicos generales y normativa vigente, a fin de contribuir con la seguridad y eficiencia de las pruebas y con la calidad de los entregables de los proyectos de la empresa usuaria. Técnico / Bachiller o cursando últimos ciclos de universidad en Contabilidad
Office Intermedio
